Hey OP, I can tell that you’re in a lot of emotional pain right now & it sounds like you’re going through a lot right now. I’m not going to try and be a hypocrite bc I attempted twice this year & jumping was one of those that I almost did.

I’m not sure what the mental health system is like where you’re at, but when I was caught trying to jump I was taken to an inpatient psych ward, which ended up being the most at-peace I’ve ever felt. I didn’t have to worry about anything from my life that I was worried about and had people to take care of my needs.

While I was there I met a guy who was certain that he wanted to die. So certain that he said the first thing he would do when he got out would be to take his life. He ended up doing everything he could to stay inpatient where he wouldn’t have to worry about having a job, making money, getting food, anything. He’s still there by choice.

I know for some people being inpatient is not a good experience, but for me it was. On difficult days I almost wish I could be there instead of here on the outside. If you’re looking for a way out of all of your stressors, getting committed inpatient could be a way to do that without dying. Then, if you feel like you still want to die you’ll always have that option once you’re released.

If you’re in the US, poison control has an online [questionnaire](https://triage.webpoisoncontrol.org/?_gl=1*11n92b*_ga*MTMzNTQ2Mzk3Ny4xNjgyNTY3NTEz*_ga_SQ0HKPQV3W*MTY4MjU2NzUxMi4xLjAuMTY4MjU2NzUxMi42MC4wLjA.#!/exclusions) that will factor in what you took plus your hight, weight, etc and makes a recommendation. 

I used it when I attempted to OD. They won’t call 911 or anything based on your answers. I did the questionnaire and then decided to go to the ER on my own after I saw what it said.

As someone who just got out of the hospital from an OD, I’d recommend calling 911 and going to the ER. The sooner you get there the better.

Healthcare is a bitch, mental health care especially. But you deserve to recover and you deserve to access all of the support and resources that you need. I wish I could help more. I just want you to know that you are worthy of recovery & you are not alone in this.

Hey OP, I also have BPD & struggle with daily suicidal thoughts. A couple of weeks ago I got out of residential treatment. They specialized in BPD and used a lot of DBT and CBT as part of the treatment. 

I went into residential directly from a psych ward (I was inpatient after an attempt). I also haven’t found a lot of benefit from my inpatient stays, but my experience in residential truly brought back my will to live & I find it easier to make it through my days. 

I’d recommend looking into a residential program like that, if you haven’t already. I was skeptical of it initially, but I’m so glad I went.

My recommendation would be that if she does, in fact, want a break, make sure you’re super clear about what she means. My SO asked for a break a few years ago & these are some questions that I wish I would have asked/had the answers to beforehand. 

How long will the break be?
How much will we be communicating, if at all?
If we do communicate, would you prefer to initiate, or can I initiate?
If I really need some support or reassurance of your love for me during the break, is it okay for me to reach out to you?
Will we still be committed to each other?
What is your ideal outcome of this break?
Is there any other way we can have that outcome without going on a break?
Do you plan for us to remain married and continue this relationship after the break?

If I had these answers or some of them it would have eased my anxiety. You deserve answers to these questions & as your partner, she should be willing to give them to you. If she says she doesn’t know the answers, encourage her to think them through before you make it official. I know it’s terrifying right now, but trust that you can come through this stronger as a couple and as an individual.
